title: Attribute-based KMS Assertion Middleware and Timebound RBAC + Audit Proxy
author: Leah Morgan
description: Motivation: customers operating in regulated jurisdictions requested stronger proofs of KMS usage plus tighter operator grants to reduce blast radius during forensics. This PR introduces an attribute-based KMS assertion middleware that issues short-lived signed assertions (X-Redwood-KMS-Assertion) tied to operator attributes and request residency hints, plus an audit-proxy that canonicalizes and deduplicates multi-region audit forwards. The goal is conservative enforcement: assertions are required for CMK-scoped calls, and RBAC v2 policies can reference assertion claims to grant timebound operator privileges. Changes include a small runtime middleware, a lightweight assertion signer/verifier service, RBAC policy templates and a migration shim for legacy audit exports. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4218), [x] unit + integration tests, [x] policy templates for rbac-policy-bundle, [x] migration shim for older audit-forwarders, [x] e2e in canary region. Backwards compatibility: non-assertion calls are accepted if the tenant has feature-flag disabled; the middleware emits warnings and a deprecation metric. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 50% main -> full with automatic enforcement during a scheduled maintenance window. See linked linear and SUP-887 for support playbook and postmortem criteria.

release_notes: Adds attribute-based KMS assertions (X-Redwood-KMS-Assertion) and a canonicalizing audit-proxy. Administrators can enable enforcement via feature-flag; includes migration guide and RBAC v2 policy templates for timebound operator grants.
notes_for_ops: Canary deployed to region-us-west-2 for 72h. Key runtime knobs: assertor.signer_key_path, assertion.max_ttl_seconds (default 300), rbac.assertion_cache_ttl_ms (default 250). If KMS unavailable, audit-proxy will buffer up to 5 minutes and emit telemetry rcpt=buffered. Follow SUP-887 playbook for tenant-impacting rollbacks.
